data.name: QuickStart.Description
data.value: PlainBytes MetadataScrubber is a lightweight Windows utility for removing metadata from Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files. It supports both individual files and batch processing.

data.name: QuickStart.Tip.Title
data.value: The simplest workflow

data.name: QuickStart.Tip.Body
data.value: Add files → Confirm the strategy → Clear Metadata

data.name: QuickStart.Step1.Title
data.value: Add Files

data.name: QuickStart.Step1.Body
data.value: After opening the app, drag the files you want to process into the main window. You can also use the file selection feature in the main window to add files. You can add multiple files at once, including files of different types. Added files will appear in the file list in the main window.

data.name: QuickStart.Step2.Title
data.value: Select a Cleanup Strategy

data.name: QuickStart.Step2.Body
data.value: After adding files, the main window shows the cleanup strategy currently in use. In most cases, you can simply use the Default Strategy. If the files require a different cleanup scope, you can select another preset strategy from the main window.

data.name: QuickStart.Step3.Title
data.value: Start Cleaning

data.name: QuickStart.Step3.Body
data.value: After confirming the files and strategy, click Clear Metadata. The app will automatically process the files in the list. Progress is displayed while processing, and controls related to the current task are temporarily disabled. The results are displayed when processing is complete.

data.name: QuickStart.Step4.Title
data.value: Quick Actions from the Context Menu

data.name: QuickStart.Step4.Body
data.value: If you don't need to open the main window, you can use the context menu directly from Windows File Explorer. Available actions: Clear Metadata (Default Strategy), View Metadata, and Clean with Another Strategy. The context menu is designed for quick access; the main window remains the primary interface for the full feature set.

data.name: Overview.Description
data.value: MetadataScrubber provides the following key features.

data.name: Overview.Card1.Title
data.value: Clear Metadata

data.name: Overview.Card1.Body
data.value: Remove metadata that may be contained in Office and PDF files. Batch processing is supported.

data.name: Overview.Card2.Title
data.value: View Metadata

data.name: Overview.Card2.Body
data.value: Click a file in the main window to expand and view the metadata currently detected in that file. Viewing metadata does not modify the file.

data.name: Overview.Card3.Title
data.value: Cleanup Strategies

data.name: Overview.Card3.Body
data.value: Use preset strategies to define the cleanup scope. There is no need to configure individual fields for each file.

data.name: Overview.Card4.Title
data.value: Batch Processing

data.name: Overview.Card4.Body
data.value: Add multiple files and process them together. When processing is complete, the app displays the number of successful and failed files, along with reasons for failures.

data.name: Formats.Description
data.value: The following file formats are currently supported.

data.name: Formats.Card.Word.Title
data.value: Word

data.name: Formats.Card.Word.Meta
data.value: .docx

data.name: Formats.Card.Word.Body
data.value: OpenXML documents. Can process basic properties, revisions, comments, custom properties, and residual data such as template paths.

data.name: Formats.Card.Excel.Title
data.value: Excel

data.name: Formats.Card.Excel.Meta
data.value: .xlsx

data.name: Formats.Card.Excel.Body
data.value: OpenXML workbooks. Cleanup scope matches Word for the same types of metadata.

data.name: Formats.Card.Ppt.Title
data.value: PowerPoint

data.name: Formats.Card.Ppt.Meta
data.value: .pptx

data.name: Formats.Card.Ppt.Body
data.value: OpenXML presentations. Cleanup covers basic properties, revisions and comments, and residual path information.

data.name: Formats.Card.Pdf.Title
data.value: PDF

data.name: Formats.Card.Pdf.Meta
data.value: .pdf

data.name: Formats.Card.Pdf.Body
data.value: Processes PDF Info, XMP, historical residual data, and attachments with path references. Info and XMP are two independent metadata systems and are shown separately when viewing.

data.name: Formats.Office.Heading
data.value: Office Files

data.name: Formats.Office.Description
data.value: OpenXML files created by Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are supported. The following are primarily processed: basic document properties, revision information, comment information, custom properties, residual information such as template paths, and related residual data such as thumbnails.

data.name: Formats.Pdf.Heading
data.value: PDF Files

data.name: Formats.Pdf.Description
data.value: The following are primarily processed: PDF Info metadata, XMP metadata, historical residual information in the file, and attachments with related path references. PDF Info and XMP are two independent metadata systems, so they are displayed separately when viewing metadata.

data.name: Strategies.Description
data.value: Strategies determine which categories of metadata are cleared. There is no need to configure individual fields one by one. The current cleanup scope is divided into three categories.

data.name: Strategies.Card1.Title
data.value: Basic Properties

data.name: Strategies.Card1.Body
data.value: Processes basic information such as author, company, last modified by, creation time, modified time, and total editing time.

data.name: Strategies.Card2.Title
data.value: Revisions & Comments

data.name: Strategies.Card2.Body
data.value: Processes information related to the editing process, such as revision history, comments, and comment authors.

data.name: Strategies.Card3.Title
data.value: Hidden Paths & Traces

data.name: Strategies.Card3.Body
data.value: Processes template paths, custom properties, residual thumbnail data, and PDF attachments or local path references that may reveal a file's origin.

data.name: Strategies.Default.Tip.Title
data.value: Default Strategy

data.name: Strategies.Default.Tip.Body
data.value: The app always has a Default Strategy. When you click Clear Metadata, or use Clear Metadata from the Windows context menu, the current Default Strategy is used.

data.name: Strategies.Preset.Heading
data.value: Preset Strategies

data.name: Strategies.Preset.Description
data.value: The app includes three built-in presets: External Distribution, Internal Archive, and Basic Cleanup. These cannot be modified. You can create custom strategies to meet your needs.

data.name: Faq.Q1
data.value: Why can't a file be processed?

data.name: Faq.A1
data.value: Common reasons include: the file is encrypted, the file is corrupted, you don't have permission to access the file, the file is being used by another program, or the file format is not supported. When processing fails, the app shows the number of failed files and provides the reason for each failure.

data.name: Faq.Q2
data.value: Can I process multiple files at once?

data.name: Faq.A2
data.value: Yes. You can drag multiple files into the main window and run the cleanup once for all of them. You can also select multiple files in Windows File Explorer and use the context menu.

data.name: Faq.Q3
data.value: Does viewing metadata modify the file?

data.name: Faq.A3
data.value: No. View Metadata only reads and displays the metadata currently contained in the file. It does not perform any cleanup operation.

data.name: Faq.Q4
data.value: Why might the Info and XMP metadata in a PDF be different?

data.name: Faq.A4
data.value: A PDF may contain both Info and XMP metadata. They do not necessarily contain the same information, so the app detects and displays them separately.

data.name: Faq.Q5
data.value: Can I modify the file list while cleanup is in progress?

data.name: Faq.A5
data.value: No. Controls related to the current task are temporarily locked during processing to prevent changes to the task while files are being processed.

data.name: Faq.Q6
data.value: Will failed files be silently skipped?

data.name: Faq.A6
data.value: No. Failed files are counted separately, and the corresponding reason for each failure is displayed.

data.name: CustomDev.Description
data.value: If MetadataScrubber does not cover your workflow—for example additional file types, custom metadata rules, batch cleanup automation, or a dedicated Windows utility—we can discuss custom development for file privacy, metadata processing, workflow automation, and other purpose-built solutions.

data.name: Privacy.Local.Heading
data.value: Local Processing

data.name: Privacy.Local.Description
data.value: MetadataScrubber processes file analysis and metadata cleanup locally on your device. File contents are not uploaded to any server and are not processed through cloud services.

data.name: Privacy.Original.Heading
data.value: Original Files

data.name: Privacy.Original.Description
data.value: The app only processes files that you explicitly select. Cleanup does not upload or modify any files other than those you choose.

data.name: Privacy.Tip.Title
data.value: Recommendation

data.name: Privacy.Tip.Body
data.value: For important files, we recommend keeping a backup of the original file before performing cleanup.

data.name: Tips.1.Title
data.value: Tip 1: Add Multiple Files at Once

data.name: Tips.1.Body
data.value: When you need to process multiple files, drag them into the window at the same time instead of adding them one by one.

data.name: Tips.2.Title
data.value: Tip 2: Set Your Default Strategy

data.name: Tips.2.Body
data.value: If most of your files use the same cleanup scope, set your preferred strategy as the Default Strategy. After that, you can simply click Clear Metadata.

data.name: Tips.3.Title
data.value: Tip 3: View Before Cleaning

data.name: Tips.3.Body
data.value: If you're not sure what metadata a file contains, click the file to view its metadata first, then perform the cleanup once you've confirmed what needs to be removed.

data.name: Tips.4.Title
data.value: Tip 4: Use the Context Menu

data.name: Tips.4.Body
data.value: For quick, one-off cleanup tasks, you don't need to open the app. In File Explorer: Right-click → Clear Metadata.

data.name: Tips.5.Title
data.value: Tip 5: Use Different Strategies for Different Scenarios

data.name: Tips.5.Body
data.value: If you regularly handle files for different purposes, such as external distribution and internal archiving, create corresponding preset strategies in advance and select the appropriate one when needed.
